title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded during Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco when traffic gridlock caused their batteries to drain faster than they could reach charging stations. At least a dozen vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, required towing assistance after coming to a halt on city streets. One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks debris, though no injuries were reported.

The deployment encountered conditions outside normal operating parameters: unexpected road closures, unusually heavy traffic volume, and congestion that prevented vehicles from reaching their intended destinations. The system had no mechanism to route around the disruption or to alert human operators with sufficient time to relocate vehicles before their batteries depleted. A human dispatcher or routing system with real-time traffic prediction capabilities could have intervened before vehicles became immobilized.

What is not established: whether Waymo had warned its systems would be vulnerable to such disruptions, or what specific battery capacity and route-planning assumptions the vehicles relied on.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
Multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded on San Francisco streets during Fourth of July celebrations when their batteries drained in heavy traffic following fireworks at the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets and requiring towing assistance. The company attributed the incident to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion.

The situation frustrated other motorists, with one driver reporting nearly two hours in standstill traffic. A Waymo vehicle also caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries occurred. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated plans to discuss the incident with public and private partners to improve future events. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions.
